belief: My illness, disability, or scars will last forever.
meta: A Christian look at the fear that your illness, disability, or scars will last forever, with Scripture, questions, and homework for finding hope in the truth.
origins: Living with chronic illness, pain, or disability. Physical scars from injury, surgery, or abuse. Losing abilities with age. Not knowing what Scripture says about the resurrection body. Discouragement that makes the future look like more of the same.
teaches: God promises that our bodies will be raised imperishable, glorious, and powerful. What is sown in weakness is raised in power. Isaiah foresaw the blind seeing, the deaf hearing, and the lame leaping like a deer. God says, “Behold, I make all things new,” and promises no more death, mourning, crying, or pain. Your present sufferings are real, but they are not comparable to the glory that will be revealed. Whatever you carry now is not forever.
self_statements: My body will never be whole.
There’s no hope for my body.
errors: Predicting that your present condition is permanent forever.
Turning “this is hard now” into “this will always be.”
Focusing on present pain while overlooking God’s promises.
Letting an illness or scar define who you are.
questions: What does Isaiah 35 promise for the blind, deaf, and lame?
What will happen to what is sown in weakness?
What does God promise about pain in the new creation?
How does Romans 8:18 compare present suffering with future glory?
Who am I apart from my illness or scars?
What does it mean that God makes all things new?
How can hope for the future help me today?
truth: My illness, disability, or scars will not last forever. God promises to raise my body imperishable, glorious, and powerful. In the new creation there will be no more pain. My present suffering is real, but it is not comparable to the glory that will be revealed. God will make all things new, including me.
hw_questions: What does Isaiah promise for the lame and blind?
What happens to what is sown in weakness?
What does God promise about pain?
How does present suffering compare to future glory?
Who am I apart from my condition?
What does “all things new” mean for me?
hw_truths: My present condition is not forever.
My body will be raised in glory and power.
There will be no more pain.
My suffering now is not comparable to the coming glory.
My illness or scars do not define me.
log: Each day, write one hard thing about my body and one promise about the body God will give me.
name_example: But Sarah’s citizenship is in heaven, and she eagerly awaits a Savior from there, the Lord Jesus Christ, who will transform her lowly body to be like His glorious body.
actions: and circle every promise of restoration.
Write a letter to your future, resurrected self,
describing what you look forward to.
how your condition affects you, and ask them to pray.
Find one small way to live fully today
tracker: One promise about my future body
prayer: Father, thank You that my present suffering is not forever. Help me reject the fear that my illness, disability, or scars will last forever. Thank You for the promise of a body raised in glory and power, and a world with no more pain. Give me hope and strength for today. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
